entries.errorSignature: Vercel headless deployment fails after login
entries.preventionRule: Always ensure the Vercel project is interactively linked before delegating deployment to headless CI/CD or autonomous swarm agents.
Always inject Ozone platform flags into Playwright configs when running in a Wayland environment.

entries.errorSignature: Hardcoded Supabase URL and keys in createBearerSupabaseClient
entries.preventionRule: Never commit live credentials, API keys, or JWTs. Always use environment variables and ensure client factories validate their existence.

entries.errorSignature: Kysely Pool exhaustion due to per-request instantiation
entries.preventionRule: Always enforce singleton patterns for database connection pools in serverless/server action environments to prevent connection exhaustion.

entries.errorSignature: Unreachable email validation in LoginForm.tsx blur handler
entries.preventionRule: When handling onChange or onBlur for HTML5 specific inputs (like type="email"), utilize the Constraint Validation API (e.target.validity) instead of parsing e.target.value directly.

entries.errorSignature: Deleted main-tip secrets reappear as live files on stale public bot branches (bolt/*, vercel/*, jules/*)
entries.preventionRule: After leaking or scrubbing any secret, enumerate git ls-remote --heads and grep EVERY published branch for the secret fingerprint, not just main; delete stale bot branches immediately after their work lands.
Treat 'remaining heads are clean' as an unverified claim until every published branch is fingerprint-scanned; bundle tips (with chmod 600) BEFORE any push --delete of diverged branches.

entries.errorSignature: On a public repo, rewriting refs/heads/* does NOT remove leaked secrets: refs/pull/<N>/head pins pre-rewrite commits forever, so GitHub never GCs them (71/138 PR heads still serve live Supabase JWTs)
entries.preventionRule: Deleting a branch or rewriting refs/heads/* does NOT remove a secret from a public repo: refs/pull/<N>/head pins the pre-rewrite commit forever. Treat any leaked secret as live until the key is rotated AND unreachable objects are purged server-side. Never treat push --delete, a history rewrite, or a 'heads are clean' scan as remediation.

entries.errorSignature: Regex secret fingerprinting false-positives on placeholder values; base64 token counts read as 0 unless the API's newline wrapping is stripped first
entries.preventionRule: Always tr -d '\n' before base64 -d when reading files via the GitHub contents API, and disambiguate placeholders from real secrets by comparing blob ids across commits (git rev-parse <sha>:<path>) or by spotting filler like 00000000/XXXX rather than trusting a regex match alone.
